scope: Add an exact versioned task and policy with final-stage-only concise output guidance; preserve v1-v4 requests, validation, warnings, model limits and all authority boundaries.
riskAnalysis: Guidance is a bounded experiment, not a recovered cause or guaranteed success. Exact new v5 registration inherits v4 schema, source grammar, request/token/time and accounting controls. Only chief-final instructions change; no field, warning, provenance, acceptance or publication check relaxes. Old contracts remain exact.

threatModel.assets: Immutable stage receipts and quality facts, exact source/task/release identity, review attribution, spending records and publication/acceptance restrictions.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Untrusted model prose versus backend-derived closed observations; syntactic quality versus integrity; automated technical review versus independent acceptance; data-only patch worker versus generated execution.
threatModel.abuseCases: Concise wording suppresses QA findings, Auditor rejection, quality references or uncertainty; forged final acceptance; new policy omitted from authority selectors; historical requests silently changed.
threatModel.mitigations: Exact registered v5 final-only predicate; unchanged required QA/ref and unresolved rejection checks; full controller positive and forged acceptance cases; canonical journal/serial policy integration; forty frozen request hashes and five actual v4 request/context reconstructions.

defects.rootCause: Observed v4 final HTTP200 response exhausted its 4000-output-token cap; exact partial output is absent, so reason for overgeneration is unknown. Exact-context valid synthetic final is1237bytes, proving no inherent need to raise limits.
defects.detectionGap: Fixture completion proves contract feasibility, not model output brevity or live success. Existing generic concise guidance did not prevent this one incomplete result.
defects.regression: Exact v5 final-only concise instructions, same4000final/24000aggregate limits, actual five-stage controller fixture with warnings and honest rejection, forged acceptance denial with preserved usage, forty historical request goldens and five actual v4 reconstructions.
defects.historicalPrevention: Preserve incomplete provider diagnostics and usage; distinguish controlled prompt experiment from proven historical cause, never synthesize a final result or replay consumed authority.

rollback: Disable execution, revoke grants and stop current sequence; preserve all v1-v5 requests/receipts/accounting. Revert via reviewed feature successor only, never erase history or revive approvals.

negativePaths.malformed-response: Unchanged strict schema/refs/QA and Auditor integrity reject malformed output or fabricated acceptance; incomplete max_output_tokens remains a failure with usage, not fabricated success.
negativePaths.stale-state: Exact new descriptor/policy and release/task binding, unchanged old request goldens; stale grants remain unusable.
negativePaths.concurrency: Existing serial owner controller/CAS and one-time grant controls remain; UI canonical journal routes the new exact policy without parallel dispatch or automatic retry.
negativePaths.cancellation: Existing cancellation/revocation/cleanup remains authoritative and is exercised by focused count-denial and full STRICT/Redis release coverage. No worker permission changed.
negativePaths.worker-interruption: Real restricted data-copy worker lifecycle and cleanup are unchanged; generated source stays inert and source-test permission remains unavailable for this task.
negativePaths.api-outage: Provider/count errors remain fatal with usage diagnostics, no automatic retries or fabricated stage success. Quality annotations do not replace transport evidence.
negativePaths.authorization-denial: Source/owner/workspace/grant and policy checks remain fatal; forged/cross-workspace quality receipts and model refs cannot create authority.
negativePaths.spending-limit: Existing monitoring policy and original ledger history remain unchanged, actual token usage is separate from uncertain fees; request/count/token/time ceilings remain enforced.
negativePaths.partial-execution: The failed v3 stage and observed usage are preserved. V4 quality-only observations remain inside immutable validated receipts for later critics; final outcomes explicitly prevent technical acceptance when unresolved.

proactiveReview.architecture: Same five roles, controller, journals and data-copy worker. New exact descriptor/policy preserves old contracts; final-only instruction change, no orchestration layer.
proactiveReview.dependencies: No package, credential, infrastructure or model migration. Existing authenticated task snapshot and cryptographic receipt helpers are reused.
proactiveReview.threats: Model warning suppression or forged receipt metadata must not cross the trusted review boundary; scalar source and authorization guards remain fatal.
proactiveReview.failureModes: Preserve omitted-ref, wrong-workspace/source, count denial, invalid patch, clipped narrative, final-only issue and cleanup failure evidence without claiming unobserved original text.
proactiveReview.faultInjection: Actual controller fixture runs all five stages with quality warning/rejection; forged final acceptance fails after four receipts with usage and cleanup preserved. Existing interruption/cancel/timeout coverage stays required.
proactiveReview.independentChallenge: Independent QA and Auditor checked exact final request feasibility, rejected blind limit increases and reviewed v5 narrow guidance; test-only result-shape mistake corrected without runtime relaxation.
proactiveReview.recovery: After each attempt preserve original receipts and usage, revoke grants, stop paid authority and qualify any exact successor before another distinct attempt. No consumed approval reuse.
proactiveReview.readiness: Focused source/UI/history/controller checks and independent review precede exact committed STRICT/Redis/CI/CodeQL/Browser qualification; no claim v5 live success until its receipts exist.
